post_content:
Contrasting example of customer care and how it helps build brand image. I
recently made an order of 2 burgers and chicken nuggets from The Burger Club
using Zomato app. I received 2 burgers with no nuggets. I contacted the Zomato
customer support and at the same time contacted the outlet to inform about the
missing item. The two contrasting responses- The Burger Club: executive at the
outlet admitted the mistake and sent the missing item at my place with an
additional burger to make up for the miss. The delivery executive (Burger
club's) apologised again and ensured that the same won't happen again. Zomato:
it took them 35 minutes to assign the customer support executive to look into
the matter. The executive took another half an hour to understand the whole
situation and was still clueless of what was needed to be done. And ultimately
used the golden phrase, " we apologize". Zomato should learn a lesson or two
about customer service and reward such outstanding vendors.

bring if given right direction. If you read about the biographies of prominent

the reasons for which they are remembered & honoured by the world 😊 Finding

not necessary that every such skill can be converted into passion. But

post_content:
Finally revealing my secrets on "How to stand out in a room?" / "Network the
best" I'm sure you would want everyone to remember you, love your presence,
talk about you, be eager to engage with you, know your name already before you
join an event and what not! Let me share time tips for you to network
especially when you're at an international event (could apply to normal events
too) : \- If there's probably a group, make sure you interact with all of the
posts that introduce delegates. (That way people remember you) \- Connect with
delegates on social media, talk to people with similar domain as yours and
even with who don't, you never know what you might learn. (Pre-event) \-
Appreciate the work organising team is putting in for the event. \- If you're
in a room, engage with a big smile, share your experiences. Don't stand in a
corner waiting for people to come talk to you. \- Take small gifts whenever
you're going to an event, you never know when you might find your next best
friend. \- Make plans during an event and ask other delegates to join! (Could
be an excursion, special meeting with a speaker etc.) Learn to lead. I think
Daniel Ramamoorthy knows the best. You can always ask him for more on events!
